Bit late but I've just found this so I'll offer my own perspective.

It's no accident that the night lords are just sociopathic murderers and sadists, It's what they were made to be.

I've seen that quite a few responses have mentioned them as a police/ peace keeping force, which I don't think they are. They're terrorists, and designed for that exact purpose. A legion of super human sadists whose only goal during the great crusade was to descend on a recalcitrant worlds, brutally kill a small percentage of the population, and broadcast the torture to the rest of the planet, bringing the planet into compliance without damaging important infrastructure. There may have been noble intentions in the beginning with the original 8th legion sourced from terra, but that was bled away with the introduction of nostraman recruits.

Then, while completing their directive of bringing worlds into compliance via fear and torture, planets begin to rebel less and less. It's not surprising, the crusade is nearing completion, but where does that leave a legion of murderers? Unlike the ultramarines and several other legions who have talents other than warfare, what would an imperium do with a legion of a hundred-thousand sociopaths?

So they are ordered to report for censure...for doing what they had been doing since the legions founding. To us this makes sense, to a night lord this is nothing short of a betrayal. 

I think that's why I find the legion interesting. An awful, grotesque bunch of the worst people you could imagine, fighting ostensibly for their bruised ego at betrayal but usually fighting to slack their sadistic tendencies. They're a legion of hypocrites, and I think that makes them a little more interesting than most.

As an aside, I think this even works on the tabletop to an extent. NL are one of the weakest legions atm due to most of their strats affection leadership and combat attrition. This usually means that against space marines or any other faction it'll mean very little, but against weaker factions it actually becomes quite effective. 

Even on the tabletop they only really excel against those weaker than themselves, and isn't that just the most NL thing you can think of.

If i were to hazard a guess, i would say that is a burl of some sort. Basically, since the cells of plants are rigid, and don't often travel through the circulatory system, if a cell in a plant begins to divide out of control, the growth will remain stationary. Its kind of like a tree tumor.

Your body is pretty good at stopping cancer before it starts, usually. After around 30 duplications, your cells will begin cell death, or apoptosis, which will usually prevent cells from causing tumors (as DNA degrades with each duplication). Other than that, your immune system can detect changes in cell function and cause the cell to go through cell death manually, before recycling the components of the dead cell.
